This is my first post and a true story from last Sunday. I've been in genuine shock since then, so excuse me for not posting it immediately.

Some context: I'm a guy who moved to San Francisco recently and have been staying at a budget hotel (basically a dorm/hostel). Toilets are shared and there are 2 on each floor. I'm not easily fazed and I've almost been stabbed in this city but this situation broke my brain.

It's the night after San Francisco Pride (which I loved). I am awoken at 2:30 AM by a combination of my eager bladder and some noises in the hallway, which is totally normal. I sleep naked and blind, so I can't just run out into the hallway.

After feeling around for a minute for my glasses and keys, I couldn't find either in the dark, and I really, really, had to pee. So, I gave up on finding my glasses, threw on a towel, and made my way out of my room without locking my door. I've done this a hundred times before and I knew I'd only be gone for 1 minute, so didn't even think twice. Ah...

Relived, I return down the hallway and to my room, still blind and basically naked. As I open the door, I hear strange noises coming from inside. In the dark of my room, I see what appears to be a young lady in clubby clothing rummaging through my shit. Again, I was only gone for 1 minute.

This is terrifying and unexpected so I let out a girly scream and stammer out "Wh-what the fuck?!".

The mysterious figure is equally startled and turns to me. My vision is shit but it looks like she has a man's face and soon a deep voice replies: "I was just looking for an iPhone charger".

My sleepy heterosexual lizard brain flips into confused mode because I completely forgot that trans people exist. My ears are telling me that there is a strange man in my room robbing me, my blurry eyes are telling me that there is an attractive lady (hurr durr potential sex) in my room, I'm still basically naked, and no part of this situation makes any sense.

I try to speak but instead shout: "I-I don't have a charger!" The person replies: "Oh, okay" and casually leaves as IF IT'S NO BIG DEAL. I lock the door and sit on my bed for half an hour high on adrenaline and confused about my life. Now I lock my door every. fucking. time.

TL;DR: Went to take a piss without locking my door and came back to a mysterious transgendered person browsing my room.
TIFU by not locking my door
I'm not saying I hate trans people - but I sure don't support the idea.

This person was a professional thief. The bit about the iPhone and casually leaving is just meant to confuse you enough, especially late at night when it takes a bit longer to get your thoughts together, for the person to turn that casual walk into a run the second they close your door.

I found myself in the same position some years ago. I won't mention the date or country, but we'll just say that it is a place which is known for authoritarianism and distrust of foreigners. The hotel had put me alone on a very high floor, which was weird, but who knows, right? I left a window open a bit before going to sleep. In the early hours of the morning, I (sort of) woke up with a groggy thought: "wait, something is strange. I feel a draft. The door is open for some reason." Impressive, now I think about it, that I would actually half wake up with that coherent thought at 3am or so.

I got up and noticed a shadowy profile in the door. The person said, "you're dreaming. Go back to sleep" and closed the door between us. I stood there for what seemed like 3 or 5 seconds, snapped out of it, and ran to the door. The hallway was empty. The person either booted it all the way down the hallway or had an adjoining room as safe harbour. I know that I had locked the door, so the person had a master key or other way of getting into the room. I am absolutely sure that the person was allowed into the room with the assistance of the hotel, whether it was to commit theft (which wouldn't be in the hotel's best interests in the long term) or if the country's security services thought that I was suspicious for some reason (I don't see myself as suspicious, but I'm a bit biased!).

Given that you were in San Francisco and not some backwater authoritarian shithole, I'd think that your person was just in there to steal stuff. But either way, you can see how the casual attitude can really mess with a tired mind!

Having a discussion within club about genetics v training.

What time would people consider to be achievable by any male under 50 with the right training (assume fit an healthy). I was thinking about 40-45 minutes

I would say over 15 years old as well - short legs have a long way to go.

There are many definitions of "fit and healthy". Do you mean "in proper running condition"?

I know some powerlifters that are absolutely fit and healthy - and they would struggle with a 10min mile.

I personally am a sprinter - and while I've trained hard for XC - I'm still only running ~46 minutes. I finished last track season ranked 17th in my age group in the USATF for the 200m and 19th for the 400m - so I would say I'm fairly fit and healthy.

Wait, I guess you say "with the right training" (I'll assume this includes diet, etc)

I'd say 50-60 minutes is closer to reasonable. I know most of my fellow sprinters would have to dedicate years to get the endurance necessary.

You have to factor 1 thing in, in addition to genetics - and that is early life activities.

The basis of the discussion is what can anyone who has no health issues run. Training time is unlimited, eg 6 months to 5 years+ Properly coached with no injuries.

We were essentially discussing under optimal health/training/diet what can someone achieve with "crap" genetics as opposed to "elite" genetics

Crap genetics, but still healthy can leave someone with a serious uphill battle. I'd say 10min/mi is a good mark.

My neighbor when I was growing up had a severe genetic defect that made him likely to be crippled his whole life - he doesn't grow the proper amount of muscle. His mother was very diligent and forced him to continually work out. He still works out 7 days a week... and compared to everyone else with his condition he is Hercules. Compared to you and me, he is just about average. Well into the category of "healthy" and not anywhere near the ability to run sub 10min miles.

Training (and nutrition and rest) will overcome genetics until the sub-elite level.

In high school there was a 5'2" mexican runner that was built like a lineman running mid 15 minute 5k's running next to the 6'3" white boys.

Meb and company at the elite level are 5'2" to 5'8".

So... I agree with your estimate, 40-45 is very achievable with the right training/coaching. It definitely won't be easy and won't (likely) be done without speed workouts and 5-6 days a week, but that's definitely within reach.
